ex-ŏcŭlo , āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. oculus,
I.to deprive of the eyes or sight (ante- and postclass.): “ni ei caput exoculassitis,” Plaut. Rud. 3, 4, 26 : “caecam et prorsus exoculatam esse fortunam,” eyeless, sightless, App. M. 7, p. 188, 24 ; id. ib. 207, § 8.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
